metaDescription: Door-to-door car shipping from New York: what a 75-foot rig can reach, parkway truck bans, meeting points, who signs the bill of lading, and timing windows.
h1: Door-to-door car shipping in New York
heroSub: The driver comes to you, as close as a 75-foot rig can legally and safely get. Here is how pickup actually works in the five boroughs, Long Island, Westchester, and upstate.
intro:
Door-to-door car shipping means the carrier picks the car up at your address and delivers it to the destination address, instead of making you drive to a yard on either end. It is the standard service at Big Apple Car Shipping, included in every quote with no extra fee. What people need to understand is what "door" means when the pickup vehicle is an 80,000-pound truck nearly 75 feet long. In Ohio it means your driveway. In Queens, off the Southern State, or on a hill in Westchester, it often means the big lot two blocks away.

This page explains residential car pickup in New York: the parkway and bridge restrictions, the meeting-point protocol, who needs to be present, what gets signed, and timing. Door to door auto transport is already built into the number the quote tool gives you.

sections.h2: What door-to-door car shipping means with a 75-foot rig
sections.html:
A loaded two-deck car hauler is about 75 feet long and 13 feet 6 inches tall. It needs a wide turn, no low wires or limbs, and a place to stop for 20 to 30 minutes with the ramps down. The driver's obligation is to get as close to your address as is legal and safe. In most of suburban New York that is your street or driveway. When it is not, the driver tells you where he can get to.

The alternative is terminal-to-terminal shipping, where you drop the car at a yard, often in New Jersey, and collect it at another yard near the destination. We do not make you do that. Door-to-door is how we book every load, and if the truck cannot reach your door, the meeting point is a few minutes away. Single-car flatbeds and three-car wedge trucks, which reach tighter streets, are covered on the open car transport page.

sections.h2: Why New York City and Long Island are special
sections.html:
Commercial trucks are banned from every parkway in the region: the Southern State, Northern State, Meadowbrook, Wantagh, Saw Mill River, Hutchinson River, Bronx River, Henry Hudson, Taconic, and Grand Central, plus the Belt and Cross Island. The parkways were built with stone-arch bridges as low as 7 feet 6 inches, and a 13-foot-6 car hauler would not survive the first overpass. Carriers reach Long Island by the LIE, Sunrise Highway, and Route 110, and Westchester by I-95 and I-287.

Inside the city the problems differ. Alternate-side parking means a truck cannot sit on a Brooklyn block for half an hour on a street-cleaning morning. Manhattan avenues have no room for ramps. Many Queens and Bronx streets have low wires, and dead-ends and cul-de-sacs in Nassau and Suffolk subdivisions give a semi nowhere to turn around. Gated communities and HOAs on the North Shore and in the Hamptons often refuse commercial trucks. None of this stops the shipment; it moves the pickup point. Our Bronx and Hempstead offices handle these pickups daily and know the usual spots.

When a truck cannot reach your door, the driver calls 12 to 24 hours before arrival to agree on a meeting point and time. The best spots are big paved lots with a wide entrance where a semi can pull through without backing up: shopping centers, home improvement stores, LIRR and Metro-North station lots outside rush hour, stadium lots, and the park-and-rides along the LIE and I-287. The driver suggests one on his route; if you know a better one, say so.

You drive the car to the lot, the driver loads it, and you sign the paperwork there. Plan for 30 to 45 minutes. If you live in a building with a parking garage, no car hauler can enter one, and the clearance bars at the entrance are usually under 7 feet. Bring the car to street level or to the agreed lot before the driver arrives.

sections.h2: Who needs to be there and what gets signed
sections.html:
Someone must be present at both ends: you, or an adult you authorize who has the keys and can sign. A doorman cannot sign unless you have told us in advance and he agrees to do the inspection walk-around. At pickup, the driver inspects the car and marks every existing scratch, chip, and dent on the bill of lading, which doubles as the inspection report. Walk around with him, compare it with your own photos, and sign only when you agree.

At delivery, the receiving person does the same inspection before signing. Any new damage must be written on the delivery bill of lading while the driver is still there. Payment also happens at delivery: the deposit was paid to us at booking, and the balance goes to the driver when the car comes off the truck, usually by cash, cashier's check, or Zelle depending on the carrier; confirm the method with us beforehand. The car shipping checklist covers what to have ready.

sections.h2: Delivery-side realities in Florida, California, and elsewhere
sections.html:
The same rules apply at the far end. In Florida, most snowbird deliveries go into gated communities from Boca Raton to Naples, and most gates will not admit a semi. The driver meets you at the community entrance, a nearby plaza, or the clubhouse lot if the HOA allows it. Clear the delivery with your gate office a day ahead. The New York to Florida page has lane-specific timing.

In California, hillside streets in Los Angeles, the Berkeley hills, and Marin are off limits for a long trailer, so deliveries meet at a flat lot in the valley or near the freeway. Colorado mountain towns and the historic districts of Charleston and Savannah work the same way. Wherever you are receiving the car, pick a flat lot with a wide entrance within ten minutes of the house and tell us when you book.

sections.h2: Door-to-door car shipping timing: pickup window, transit, and delivery ETA
sections.html:
You give us a first available date, and the pickup window is typically one to five days from it on busy lanes like New York to Florida or the Carolinas, sometimes longer to the Mountain West or in peak weeks. Transit is roughly three to five days to Florida and Georgia, two to four to the Carolinas and Illinois, five to seven to Texas and Colorado, and seven to ten to Arizona, California, and Washington state.

The delivery ETA is the driver's estimate and moves with weather, other deliveries on his load, and federal hours-of-service rules that cap driving at 11 hours a day. The driver calls 12 to 24 hours before delivery with a firm window. If your schedule is tight on either end, say so when booking; expedited car shipping narrows the pickup window at a premium. Door-to-door adds nothing to the price.

faqs.q: Does door-to-door car shipping cost extra?
faqs.a: No. Door-to-door is the standard service and every quote from Big Apple Car Shipping includes it. The only time a residential pickup costs more is when the street requires a smaller truck, such as a single-car flatbed for a townhouse block in Brooklyn, and we will say so up front.

faqs.q: Can a car hauler come to my house on Long Island?
faqs.a: Usually yes, if your street is reachable without a parkway and has room for a 75-foot truck to stop and turn. Many Nassau and Suffolk subdivisions with cul-de-sacs, and most gated communities, mean meeting at a nearby lot instead. The driver calls 12 to 24 hours ahead to confirm your driveway or a specific lot.

faqs.q: What if I cannot be there when the driver arrives?
faqs.a: Authorize another adult, give them the keys, and tell us their name and phone number before pickup or delivery. They walk the car with the driver, sign the bill of lading, and at delivery hand over the balance. A doorman or neighbor can do this only if arranged in advance.

faqs.q: Can the truck pick up from my apartment building's garage?
faqs.a: Almost never. Car haulers cannot enter parking garages, and the clearance bars at most New York garage entrances are under seven feet. Bring the car to street level, or drive it to the lot the driver suggests, before the agreed time. If you are away, arrange for someone with the keys to move it to the meeting point.

faqs.q: How precise is the delivery date?
faqs.a: The driver gives an ETA at pickup and calls 12 to 24 hours before arrival with a firm window of a few hours. Weather, other cars on the load, and federal driving-hour limits can shift it by a day. Transit from New York runs about three to five days to Florida and seven to ten to California.
